text: torch backend estimates column-wise noise diverges immediately raw unnormalized Gaussian-scale matrices (objective goes non-finite iteration 0; backend fails loudly rather returning garbage fit — design documented reason test suite’s registered fixture normalizes counts). Feed single-cell pipeline produces: counts, size-factor normalization, log1p, gene z-scaling.

title: Cross-cohort replication: a preregistered-style case study
text: Two cell types (T, B), 24 donors per cohort, 400 genes. Planted structure T cells: B cells carry one conserved program (genes 201-240) outcome link. predeclared hypothesis, fixed looking query cohort: T-cell program whose activity tracks outcome discovery cohort replicates sign discovery effect p < 0.05. (fitted program’s sign arbitrary; canonicalization fixes within fit, rule -sign--discovery, fixed direction.) Everything else descriptive.
code: n_genes <- 400; n_d <- 24 genes <- paste0("G", seq_len(n_genes)) mk_w <- function(idx) { w <- rep(0, n_genes); w[idx] <- rnorm(length(idx)); w } set.seed(42) w1 <- mk_w(1:40); w2 <- mk_w(61:100); w3 <- mk_w(121:160); w4 <- mk_w(201:240)  mk_cohort <- function(name, with_p3 = FALSE, p2_batch = FALSE) {   donors <- paste0(name, "_d", seq_len(n_d))   z1 <- rnorm(n_d); z2 <- rnorm(n_d); z4 <- rnorm(n_d)   batch <- sample(rep(c("b1", "b2"), each = n_d / 2))   if (p2_batch) z2 <- 1.2 * (batch == "b2") + rnorm(n_d, sd = 0.3)   y <- 0.7 * z1 + rnorm(n_d, sd = 0.8)          # outcome linked to P1   YT <- tcrossprod(z1, w1) + tcrossprod(z2, w2)   if (with_p3) YT <- YT + tcrossprod(rnorm(n_d, sd = 1.5), w3)   YT <- YT + matrix(rnorm(n_d * n_genes, sd = 0.8), n_d, n_genes)   YB <- tcrossprod(z4, w4) + matrix(rnorm(n_d * n_genes, sd = 0.8), n_d, n_genes)   colnames(YT) <- colnames(YB) <- genes   rownames(YT) <- rownames(YB) <- donors   meta <- data.frame(observation_id = donors, cohort = name, outcome = y,                      batch = batch, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)   list(data = as_cell_program_data(list(T = YT, B = YB), sample_metadata = meta),        meta = meta) } cohA <- mk_cohort("A"); cohB <- mk_cohort("B", p2_batch = TRUE) cohC <- mk_cohort("C", with_p3 = TRUE)

what: Why matched association profiles do not replicate — and what does
title: Case study: immune-aging programs across 8 global PBMC cohorts
text: natural test — correlate age betas across matched program pairs — fails every cohort (Spearman −0.07 0.17), including 981 donors beta noise negligible. cause structural, statistical: unsupervised EBMF decompositions distribute age-associated variance across K programs differently cohort (rotational freedom, adaptive shrinkage, greedy factor addition). Program identity cohort-specific even program content conserved. projection sidesteps : discovery program’s identity pinned frozen loadings, testing projected_score ~ age query asks well-posed question — fixed gene program vary age query? Replication discovery age hits (FDR < 0.05 ABF300) projected scores: Null expectation ~4%. Replication real partial — core biologically coherent programs (RTE, gd T naive, gd T Vd2 GZMK+) replicates near-universally, bulk regresses toward null winner’s-curse shrinkage projection noise.

text: Two donors x two cell types, 80 cells , 200 genes. cell type gets private marker block; everything else background Poisson noise.

text: cell type independently, package fits two-factor model Y \approx L F^T + E, Y (preprocessed) observations x genes matrix, L sample-side factors (program scores), F gene-side factors (program loadings), E residual noise. fit flashier’s empirical-Bayes matrix factorization: Greedy addition + backfitting. Factors added one time (greedy_Kmax = max_factors), new factor capturing largest remaining structured variation; greedy addition, factors jointly re-estimated (backfitting) evidence lower bound (ELBO) stops improving. nullcheck()-style pruning removes factors improve ELBO. Sparsity via empirical Bayes. factor’s loadings get point-Laplace prior (spike zero plus Laplace slab), fitted ebnm::ebnm_point_laplace. spike shrinks small loadings strongly toward zero slab admits large effects, giving programs sparse character — stored posterior means small nonzero values, exact zeros. Extract gene sets explicit loading threshold lfsr (top_genes(..., = "lfsr")), filtering exact zeros. point_normal (Gaussian slab) unimodal available alternatives. Noise model. var_type controls residual variance structure: 0 = one variance everything, 1 = one per observation (default, right pseudobulk donors differ depth/quality), 2 = one per gene, c(1, 2) = Kronecker rank-one. default selected full-factorial tuning benchmark (see README). Preprocessing. center = TRUE centers gene (default); scale = TRUE also scale unit variance (default — raw program amplitudes kept). features = "variable" restricts fit top n_variable_genes variable genes per cell type. covariate_mode = "residualize" (hard): pseudobulk matrix residualized covariate design (e.g. sequencing institute, sex) ordinary least squares factorization. Programs fit covariate-free residual expression. covariate_mode = "fixed" (soft, SOFA-style): covariate columns enter factorization fixed sample-side factors unshrunk gene effects, initialized OLS; free programs added greedily alongside everything except fixed columns backfit. covariate part returned separately (fixed_L, fixed_F) never appears program extraction. Degenerate inputs. Genes identically zero preprocessing dropped; cell type informative genes records K = 0 fit instead failing analysis. fitted object stores, per cell type, posterior means posterior SDs factor matrices (L_pm/L_psd, F_pm/F_psd), ELBO trajectory, gene panel used. Major functionality cellprograms package: as_cell_program_data() Build validated pseudobulk data object (named list observations x genes matrices, one per cell type) fit_celltype_programs() Fit per-cell-type programs EBMF backend (hard residualization soft fixed covariate adjustment; flashier cebmf_torch backend) freeze_preprocessing() / project_programs_to_cells() Freeze fit’s preprocessing spec (MR-0) project new samples onto programs unit-checked oracle assess_program_stability() Subsampling stability recovered programs, explicit accounting failed refits canonicalize_programs() Align program sign, scale labels across cell types program_scores() Sample x program activity matrix across cell types program_loadings() Gene x program loading matrix top_genes() Top-loaded genes single program, optional lfsr program_summary() Per-cell-type summary: number programs, R2, ELBO find_coordinated_programs() Detect coordinated multicellular programs (CMPs) family-wise error control within-strata donor permutation cmp_scores() Donor x CMP consensus scores annotate_cmp_tf() TF footprint every member program CollecTRI regulons (competitive + self-contained tests) cmp_triage() One-row-per-CMP triage: recurrent genes, nuisance counts, context association, replication, shared TFs program_sharing() Classify matched programs shared, partial, private (mashr loading posteriors) artifact_genes() / flag_artifact_genes() Mask V(D)J donor-genotype artifact genes simulate_pseudobulk() Simulation planted programs ground truth

what: Numerically degenerate programs, two kinds: 1. flashier can retain factors whose loadings underflow to numerical noise (median |loading| many orders of magnitude below the cell type's strongest program; e.g. sparse factors whose support is a few genes and whose remaining entries sit at ~1e-16). Their posterior SDs underflow as well, producing garbage z-scores, and correlation-based matching is scale-invariant, so they spuriously match every strong program. 2. Fixed, never-updated factors: real-scale loadings whose posterior SD column collapsed to machine precision (observed for the smallest cell type in both real cohorts). Point estimates without usable uncertainty: mashr cannot assess them. A program is degenerate when median |loading| < `rel_tol` x the cell type's largest, or when its median posterior SD (scaled to the loadings) is <= `sd_floor`. — .degenerate_programs
